questions.question: Explain the difference between circular queue and circular array implementation in Queues.
questions.ideal_answer: circular queue and circular array implementation differ in several ways: circular queue is array-based ring buffer (works by efficient space utilization) whereas circular array implementation is modulo indexing (works by preventing linear overflow). circular queue is typically used for front and rear pointers modulo capacity, while circular array implementation is used for (front + i) % capacity for ith element. Example demonstrating circular queue: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity; front = (front + 1) % capacity;. Example demonstrating circular array implementation: int front = 0, rear = 0, count = 0;.

questions.question: Explain the difference between BFS traversal and sliding window maximum in Queues.
questions.ideal_answer: BFS traversal and sliding window maximum differ in several ways: BFS traversal is breadth-first search (works by level-order graph/tree traversal) whereas sliding window maximum is deque-based optimization (works by O(n) maximum in every window). BFS traversal is typically used for queue for frontier, visited set, while sliding window maximum is used for maintain decreasing deque of indices. Example demonstrating BFS traversal: queue.offer(start); while (!queue.isEmpty()) { Node curr = queue.poll(); for (Node neighbor : curr.neighbors) if (!visited.contains(neighbor)) queue.offer(neighbor); }. Example demonstrating sliding window maximum: while (!deque.isEmpty() && arr[i] >= arr[deque.peekLast()]) deque.pollLast(); deque.offerLast(i);.
